title: Upkeep: SC-040, SC-047
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The broad rule 'no request header ever supplies scheme, host or client identity' was not widened to the bare X-Forwarded. The design only changes the narrow rule, which already applies to every non-test Go file.

Holes pinned as quiet rows or named in the because-texts, not closed: a flag after an escaped \t inside an interpreted string (acc-br-q010); a flag at the start of a later line of a raw string (acc-br-q011); an alias of the os package; client-identity names that match no shape, such as X-Envoy-External-Address (fwn-q012). Underscore spellings (HTTP_X_FORWARDED) and syscall.GetEnvironmentVariable are not named in the because-texts and have no rows, because the census that held them was removed.
internal/fitnessrules/** matches no architecture block's globs, so the package has no owner in the record. A person should say which block owns it, or whether none does.

Fitness op=check, which uses a real YAML parser, was not run here: the builder has no such tool and this machine has no PyYAML. The edited because-texts stay single-quoted and use no apostrophes, the new plain scalars have the same shape as the old ones, and TestFitnessYAMLPlainScalarsParse passes. The engine should still run op=check on the tree.

deviation: Rule 3 uses \.Environ\b instead of the prescribed \.Environ\(\). It is a superset that also catches the method taken as a value, which the rule's own because-text promises to match; dt-env-f009 pins it and dt-env-q006 pins that .Environment stays quiet.

deviation: The finding's 'line 456' and 'line 457' are stale. The narrow rule's patterns are at lines 460 and 461, and the prescribed regexes are applied to them, with the optional socket-?ip added. fwn-f030 pins it.

deviation: The separate class census (a new JSON file with its own test and loader) was dropped because the engine refused the batch as too large. The class corpus is the existing rule_spellings.json. The census names dropped with it that no kept row covers include Cloudflare's -IPv4 and -IPv6 versions in upper and lower case, X-Client-IPv4, Fastly-Client-IP, DO-Connecting-IP and Incap-Client-IP.
not reached: the running application -- a minor-lane batch is judged by its tests, not by using it
